agent_position: G1: the workflow graph as tracked data (nodes, exits, joins, guards named in a file), interpreted by the computation, with guards implemented in code
owner_disposition: G2: the graph as an explicit table in code, which gives most of the benefit with few changes; a durable change to the workflow is an OpenSpec change, so data-driven topology buys little, and interventions are per-change irregular transitions through deliberate mechanisms; the formal graph serves diagrams, specifications, and the anticipated extraction of the workflow system into its own repository
summary: The workflow graph is an explicit table in code, not a data file

agent_position: I2: interactive runs go through the wrapper in an interactive mode with a session id it chooses; the skill writes its outcome to a file the wrapper names, and the wrapper records it on exit, or a stop when it is missing
owner_disposition: I1, conditional on the session id being available to a command the session runs: the skill records its own outcome with a record command; Claude Code exports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID to every shell command it spawns (found in the installed 2.1.306 and 2.1.311 binaries), so the condition holds, and interactive steps stay plain sessions with nothing wrapped around them
summary: An interactive step records its own outcome through a record command that reads the session id from the shell

agent_position: agree: a direction reaching a node with no edge had no defined guard source; proposed guards on nodes as entry guards, checked on every entry including directions, with waives naming one of them
owner_disposition: an owner direction is not denied by any guard; a problem it causes is the owner's error; waives removed, waivers become plain directions, guards stay on step exits, the node table is added to D1
summary: Owner directions check no guard; guards apply only to step exits

agent_position: agree: the legacy reader and a new triage awaiting its outcome see the same inputs; proposed telling old triage files from new by ## Next's first words, then a committed migrate command with a log format line
owner_disposition: convert every in-flight change's records to the new format as a task of this change; no migrate command is committed and nothing tells formats apart, since after the task every change is in the new format
summary: Older records are converted once as a task of the change; no legacy reader, command, or format check

agent_position: partly: the phase-order MUST and two existing entry checks (pre-closeout validation, archive cleanup's archive) contradict D5; recommended B, the archive boundary refused at write time in both directions and other entry checks taking the direction as their override
owner_disposition: revises 13-design F1: B, with entry guards distinguished from exit guards: exit guards sit on edges and a direction bypasses them; entry guards sit on nodes and deny starting a step that cannot carry out its work, and some cannot or should not be bypassed
summary: Entry guards on nodes, some unwaivable, are checked against directions; exit guards are not

agent_position: agree: a change on another branch runs the older tooling until it merges the new code, so a one-off conversion has no safe point; recommended a committed convert command run when a change takes the new code, with detection of older log shapes, both temporary
owner_disposition: revises 13-design F2: A, a committed convert command and the computation detecting older log shapes, removed by a later change
summary: Records are converted by a committed command when each change takes the new code; older log shapes are detected, not misread
